Having a PC forces you to think about whether your hardware will support a game.

Not necessarily. While that's the case at present, there's no reason Steam couldn't automatically check your hardware and display a nice simple tick/cross next to the requirements. (If purchasing a game from the client.)

Then you must optimize a game's settings if you cannot max them out.

Plenty of games automatically set their defaults based on the hardware available.

The real difference between console and PC is one of control - the console makers impose certain restrictions to ensure a minimum standard of usability, performance, etc. There's no centralized control with PC games, so you get more variety (e.g. indie games), but you also get more variability in terms of quality, polish, etc. That's also why you see so many poorly done console ports - because the console makers insist on a certain amount of polish, but there's no such requirement for the PC release.
